description: Bottleneck: 90% of baseline is cuSOLVER's latency-bound geqr2 panel kernel. Replace QR entirely with CholeskyQR2 (R=chol(A^T A), Q=A R^-1, repeated twice for orthogonality) using TF32 tensor-core batched torch.bmm/cublas, then reconstruct the compact Householder (H,tau) from the orthogonal Q via LAPACK orhr_col-style sign-corrected unit-triangular reconstruction so householder_product(H,tau)==Q. Benchmark inputs are well-conditioned dense, so CholeskyQR2 hits FP32 tolerance. This is the GEMM-only algorithmic bet.

Bottleneck: at small n (shapes 0,1,2: n=32/176/352, batch 20/40/40) cuSOLVER per-launch overhead dominates (~16us per 32x32 QR). Write a custom load_inline CUDA kernel: one threadblock factors one matrix entirely in shared memory via classic Householder QR, producing H/tau directly, batched across all matrices in a single launch. n=176 (124KB) fits B200 smem; column-tile n=352. Eliminate the launch storm.

Bottleneck: trailing-update GEMMs run on SIMT FP32 cores (cutlass3x_sm100_simt_sgemm), leaving TF32 tensor cores (~500 TFLOP/s) idle. Implement blocked Householder QR from scratch: factor a b-column panel (b=32/64), form the compact-WY T factor, apply the block reflector to the trailing matrix via cuBLAS GEMM with CUBLAS_TF32_TENSOR_OP_MATH. Maximize the tensor-core trailing fraction; produce native H/tau. Sweep block size.

Bottleneck: compute throughput at large n (shapes 4,5,6: n=1024/2048/4096). FP32 SIMT leaves BF16 tensor cores (~2 PFLOP/s) idle. Implement blocked Householder QR whose panel and trailing updates use BF16/FP16 tensor-core GEMM (WMMA or cublas) with FP32 accumulation, exploiting the loose factor tolerance (20*n*eps32 ~1e-2 at n=4096). Add one FP32 correction sweep if orthogonality fails. Produce valid H/tau.

Bottleneck: shape 3 (batch=640, n=512, cond=2) is 1.07M us = 96% of summed benchmark time and the leaderboard-critical case. Specialize hard for 512x512: a persistent batched kernel that keeps each 512x512 panel resident in shared/registers across the factorization, using warp-level Householder with cooperative-groups reductions, one CTA (or a few) per matrix, 640 matrices in one launch. Target this shape's geomean contribution above all else.

Bottleneck: insufficient level-3 BLAS exposure in the unblocked panel. Implement recursive Householder QR (Elmroth-Gustavson): split columns in half, factor left half recursively, update right half with the compact-WY block reflector via one large tensor-core GEMM, recurse. This casts ~all work as GEMM and naturally maximizes tensor-core utilization at every level. Build with cuBLAS TF32. Emit native compact H/tau.

Bottleneck: launch overhead + serialization across the batch dimension. Bind cuSOLVER directly via load_inline: try cusolverDnSgeqrfBatched if available, else cusolverDnXgeqrf with multiple CUDA streams so independent matrices in the batch factor concurrently (esp. batch=640 n=512 and batch=40 cases). Compare against a CUDA-graph-captured replay to kill per-iteration launch latency. Output matches geqrf H/tau natively (no reconstruction needed).

Bottleneck: the panel factorization is the critical path. Implement a Modified Gram-Schmidt QR with reorthogonalization fully in custom CUDA, fusing the column-normalize and rank-1 trailing projection into tensor-core GEMV/GEMM batches, one launch over the whole batch; then convert the resulting orthonormal Q + upper R into compact Householder (H,tau) via sign-corrected reconstruction. MGS-2 reaches FP32 orthogonality on these well-conditioned inputs. Distinct from CholeskyQR (W0) in numerics.

Branch off W5's global best (recursive-QR dispatcher, 7894us 5.66x). Its ONLY weak shapes are the large single matrices it punts to torch.geqrf: (8,2048)=1.89x and (2,4096)=tie. Profile (2,4096) under this commit, then replace the n>=2048 fallback with a custom TF32 tensor-core blocked Householder QR: panel width 64-128, compact-WY T factor, trailing update via cuBLAS GEMM with CUBLAS_TF32_TENSOR_OP_MATH (tol at n=4096 is 20*4096*eps32~1e-2, ample for TF32). Keep W5's small/mid-n recursive dispatch untouched. Emit native compact H/tau.

Continue your champion (7894us 5.66x). Your own profile says the (640,512) shape is now 66% SIMT-FP32 trailing-update GEMMs that are LAUNCH-BOUND, not throughput-bound. So cut launch COUNT, not precision: capture the recursion's fixed sequence of trailing-update + panel launches into a CUDA graph (torch.cuda.CUDAGraph or cudaGraph capture) and replay it per benchmark iter, and/or widen the recursion base/panel so fewer, larger batched GEMMs cover the trailing update.
